subject: Clarify: default storage window for prompts vs outputs (EU residency)
messages:
From: Alex Sullivan <alex.sullivan@finova.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finova.com
Date: 2026-10-20T09:14:00Z
Subject: Questions on default retention / residency for prompts & outputs

Hi Irene,

Hope you can help — we're filling out the security section of our vendor intake for Redwood and need to be specific about default data retention behavior. A few quick clarifications: 

- Do prompts (request payloads) and model outputs (generated responses) get stored by default for hosted accounts? If so, what is the default storage window for each?
- For accounts with EU residency set, does all persisted data stay in EU-only regions (including backups)?
- How do you classify "generated outputs" — are they considered derivative artifacts or part of the request record?
- If we need a guaranteed deletion for a customer record, what is the API / workflow and expected timeline?
- Any guidance on PII minimization/redaction we should include in our questionnaire?

I've attached our procurement questionnaire (procurement_questionnaire.pdf) — we're under a slightly tight timeline so an answer today or a call would be great.

Thanks,
Alex
Security & Procurement
Finova Bank
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Sullivan <alex.sullivan@finova.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention / residency for prompts & outputs

Alex — thanks for the clear questions. High-level answers below; I attached a short retention matrix and our SOC2 summary for your procurement packet. If you want, we can walk through line-by-line on a quick call.

Summary (defaults for hosted Redwood accounts):
- Prompts (request payloads): by default, request payloads and associated request metadata are retained for 60 days. These are used for debugging, billing, and quality monitoring.
- Model outputs (generated responses): default retention is 30 days for generated outputs (we treat them as derived artifacts distinct from the original request).
- Conversation transcripts (chained sessions): retained by default for 60 days unless the customer toggles "ephemeral session" at the project level.
- KV cache / live inference cache: ephemeral in-memory caches persist only for the session (typical TTL ~6 hours) and are not written to persistent logs by default.

Residency and backups: 
- If your account is configured for EU residency, persistent storage and primary backups are kept within EU regions. Disaster recovery replicas are also restricted to EU locations unless a customer opts into cross-region replication for resilience (opt-in only).
- Snapshots used for fault recovery may have delayed deletion semantics; see the delete/runbook attachment for deletion windows for backups.

PII and classification: 
- We consider generated outputs to be derivatives; however, they can contain customer-supplied PII. By default we do not perform automatic redaction — we recommend customers either (a) use client-side redaction before sending sensitive fields, or (b) enable our data-minimization presets that mask known identifier patterns.

Deletion workflow: 
- Immediate removal requests are accepted via our Data Deletion API or by opening a support case referencing the account id and descriptors. The API triggers an orchestrated purge: primary store wipe is typically completed within 72 hours (business days), followed by background purge of caches and related indexes within 30 days.

I'll let Karthik add the tech specifics on backups and the exact API call shape. Kimberly — I added you for the approved customer-facing language.

Best,
Irene
Director, Security Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Data_Retention_Matrix.xlsx, SOC2_Audit_Summary.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Sullivan <alex.sullivan@finova.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T13:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention / residency for prompts & outputs

Alex — quick technical addendum to Irene's summary:

- API delete endpoint: POST /v1/accounts/{account_id}/data:delete with body referencing selectors (session_id, user_id, date-range). A successful request returns a purge-job id. Use GET /v1/purge-jobs/{id} to track state.
- Deletion guarantees: primary data stores are cleared within 72 hours. Because of replication and backup windows, we provide a completion certificate when the purge-job reaches "complete" which indicates primary and indexed records have been removed; physical backup media may have longer retention as part of our DR policy (typically up to 90 days for snapshot retention but limited to the account's region for EU-residency accounts).
- Backups & snapshots: for EU-residency tenants, snapshots are retained in EU zones only. Snapshots are on a rolling retention schedule and wiped per the runbook; emergency restore snapshots are rare and access-controlled — we log all restore access.
- Telemetry & aggregated logs: we aggregate telemetry for platform health and remove request-level identifiers after 30 days for telemetry pipelines. PII is excluded from those aggregates by default.

Operational notes: if you need a strict contractual limit (e.g., legal requirement to purge within X hours), our Private and Dedicated offerings allow you to control retention/purge guarantees more tightly — we can provide contractual language for the SOW.

Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Sullivan <alex.sullivan@finova.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention / residency for prompts & outputs

Alex — adding customer-facing language you can paste into the questionnaire: 

"By default, Redwood persists request payloads and associated metadata for 60 days and generated outputs for 30 days. Customers can configure shorter retention or enable ephemeral sessions where transcripts are not persisted. For accounts configured with EU residency, all persistent stores and backups are maintained in EU locations unless cross-region replication has been explicitly enabled. Deletion requests can be initiated via Redwood's Data Deletion API or by raising a support case; primary purges typically complete within 72 hours with background cleanup finishing within 30 days. For customers with strict regulatory requirements, Redwood offers Dedicated and Private deployment options that permit contractual retention and purge windows."

One legal note: while we operate EU-only storage for EU tenants, certain third-party dependencies (e.g., telemetry processors) may receive anonymized metadata as part of platform operations — we provide assurances and contractual protections for any third-party subprocessors.

Next steps: if you share the completed questionnaire, we will return a redlined response within 48 hours and can schedule a 30-minute technical call tomorrow morning. I've attached our EU delete runbook and SOC2 summary for your security team.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance
Redwood Inference
